lines: All five tabs fit the panel now: Stage is no longer cut off at the right.
Copy brief is always in the Notes tab, greyed out until there's a note.
Pausing right after a design loads no longer breaks the stage.
The first time a browser opens home, What's new starts as read, so a new install opens on the shelf.
Atelier is on the gen UI kit now: light and dark (Theme at the foot of home's sidebar, or Stage › Look), solid panels and controls, the kit's sizes and motion.
Glass panels are still there: Stage › Look › Panels › Glass.

Notes are Annotate now (N): point at the design and the element under the pointer is outlined and named; click it, drag an area, or shift-click several. A bar at the top shows the moves and Copy brief with the count.
Frost: the panel and the timeline are frosted glass over the wallpaper again, in light and dark. Stage › Look › Panels picks Solid, Frost or Glass.
Annotate names a button by its words (button “Start”), skips a design's glow layers to the element under them, and outlines nothing over plain background.
While annotating, hints (picked, drawing, editing words) show in the bar at the top, and the stage keeps that strip clear so the bar never covers a design.
A line added to Taste scrolls into view where it landed.
Note pins are a raised blue disc in a dark comment shape, its corner on the spot noted; ⇧ picks look the same.
Edit CSS: every value is a field. Drag a name sideways to scrub it (⇧ for tens), double-click it to put the value back; colours take a hex too.
Home's pane: a design stands on its earlier iterations, and a phone keeps a phone's corners.
A note's picture on a phone design shows what you picked again: it was drawn about 50px too high, without the status bar's room.

Home opens in a new view, Columns (Grid is next to it at the top right): one column per folder, like Finder. One click on a project shows its newest design live in the pane beside it, with its designs and iterations as chips, how it's coded, who made it, its source, and Open, Remix, Edit.
Set `"stack"` in a project's project.json to say how it's coded; otherwise Atelier reads it from the folder.
The pages in a folder sit lower, inside it.
Home is a little bigger all round and set in one typeface at regular weight; Grid's folders and cards are one size at any window width.
A prototype's tour now runs on the timeline's clock: pause stops it at once, and dragging the timeline shows the step as it is at that moment, paused or not, forward or back.

There is no agent inside Atelier any more. Send to agent, /try takes, the critic, Pick and Instead… are gone. Copy brief is the one button: paste it into your own Claude session, and the version it makes shows beside the original.
A note is one layer: the words sit on the card, with 12 corners, 16 around and 12 between rows. The mic is gone.
Home has a new look, picked from 28 versions: neutral greys with no blue tint, no wallpaper and no screenshots.
A folder is the one object on the shelf: grey glass with pages standing in it that name what's inside. Point at it and they rise.
A project or a design is a card set in type: its name large, its facts small. Nothing is a picture of the UI.
Folders go as deep as you like. New folder makes one; drag a project or a folder onto a folder to move it; double-click a folder's name at the top to rename it.

A project's page has its context (click to write), its docs, and its designs. A design's iterations are chips under its card: pick one, then click the card to open it or Remix to copy a brief for your agent.
A design doesn't have to be made in Atelier. `atelier publish <project> --title … --open <url>` adds any prototype.
The magnifier at the top left searches the shelf (or press /). `atelier shelf`, `atelier folder` and `atelier move` do the same from the terminal.
Draw on a note: pen, ellipse, rectangle and arrow, in blue. The agent gets the drawing and what it's on.
In note mode, double-click words to edit them in place. Return notes the old and new words for the agent.
Edit CSS on a cut element: change its spacing, type, colour or radius right on screen, and the note carries old → new.
Dictate a note: the mic in the note types what you say.
⌘Return in a note sends just that note to the agent, now. Return still only saves.
The note editor reads in order: your words first, a small picture, quiet tools, Edit CSS folded away, and Send the one blue button. A blank picture is left out.
Take names, the Pick button and rank badges are medium weight now, not semibold.
Send to agent, Pick and the other main buttons are a blue tint now, never white.
Atelier works with any coding agent: Claude Code by default, or ATELIER_AGENT=gemini, codex, or your own. The button is Send to agent now.
The critic's top take is a faint blue tint now, not a blue ring.
A refresh opens the newest version of what you were looking at. Comparing keeps your older picks.
Screens stay centred: a sideways scroll on the wallpaper no longer nudges them, and a refresh always lands centred.
A note on a design that frames a live page now keeps a real picture of the page, not an empty frame.
Pause stops everything, mid-step too. In note mode the wheel scrolls the design, ⌥ lets you use it, and notes land on the element in a live page, not on its frame.
Notes are the only way to ask now. `/try 3` in a note gives three takes on just that part.
Taste learns from each design's whole run, first version to latest. Re-read all in the Taste tab.
Colour picker, dropdowns and folding groups in the Design tab.
⌥N pins a note on Atelier itself, for Claude to fix.
Takes waiting for a pick show on the vault's Today, under Needs you.
Type `atelier` in any terminal: opens it, and starts it if it isn't running.
